$comment: Reviewed decisions for production-dependency advisories (not applicable, or accepted until a date). Read by scripts/ci/audit-check.mjs: an advisory missing here, or past its expiry, fails the audit job. Re-review on expiry; remove ids the job reports as stale.

entries.reason: APPLIES, accepted for now: a large array sent to a schema without a length cap makes zod allocate one issue per failing element until the process runs out of memory. Our hub and computer validate network input with zod (tRPC inputs, REST bodies, computer frames), mostly from authenticated callers. The fix (4.6.6) was published 2026-10-11, so the 30-day minimumReleaseAge holds it back until 2026-11-10.

APPLIES, accepted for now: one gzip request with trailing bytes crashes the process. express.json() (default inflate) parses the hub's /mcp and agent-hook bodies; the desktop hub binds 127.0.0.1, an exposed standalone hub is reachable. The fix (2.4.0) was published 2026-10-22, so the 30-day minimumReleaseAge holds it back until 2026-11-21.
Via @electron/get, the electron package's install-time downloader; never in the app or hub.

APPLIES, accepted for now: one request to /mcp can exhaust hub memory. Only authenticated callers reach /mcp (and only local processes on the desktop hub, which binds 127.0.0.1). The fix (1.32.0) was published 2026-10-02, so the 30-day minimumReleaseAge holds it back until 2026-11-01; Renovate opens the bump then.

MCP SDK client-side (OAuth client, redirects), experimental-tasks and SDK bearer-auth advisories: we run only an McpServer over streamable HTTP behind our own bearer gate. ajv: the $data option is not used.
Fixed only in Electron >= 42; the 41 line gets no further patches. Clears with the Electron major upgrade.
Inside posthog-js (0.4.8, pinned by posthog): the advisory is in unzipSync (ZIP64 parsing), which posthog-js does not ship; it only compresses outgoing event batches.

NEEDS REVIEW: dompurify 3.4.15 via mermaid and 3.4.16 via @slayzone/editor. These ids were previously covered by the posthog-js entry, whose rationale (posthog's pinned 3.3.1 copy) does not apply to these paths; moved here unchanged when posthog-js 1.434 dropped dompurify.

Via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk: our server transport uses only @hono/node-server getRequestListener (no serveStatic, JSX, CORS, cookie or JWT code); the rate-limit/IP code is in the SDK auth router, which we do not mount; no URI-based security decisions.

Express internals: `trust proxy` is never set (re-check if it ever is); no route uses sequential optional groups or multiple wildcards; Express 5's default query parser is not qs; no urlencoded parser; body limits are valid.
Convex auth (convex/auth.ts) uses the GitHub OAuth provider only: no email provider, no getToken() call, a single OAuth provider.
Counted as production only because better-auth lists vitest as an optional peer; dev tooling in practice. Our Vite dev servers bind localhost, and the dev-server advisories need --host.
Via @tailwindcss/typography: runs at build time on our own CSS.
Via @lobehub/icons / @lobehub/ui: we deep-import 6 icon components, which do not load these.
Via archiver in the CLI zip export: no glob patterns are passed.
The crash needs an argument whose toString is not a function; only our own calls reach it.
better-auth merges its own config objects; the pollution needs attacker-controlled input as the first argument.
Via pbf's .proto compiler; electron-chrome-web-store only uses pbf's runtime decoder on the CRX header.
